options: A single server inside a data center
A specific geographic area where a provider operates a cluster of data centers
A virtual network with no physical location
A billing category for cloud resources
questions.explain: A region is a specific geographic area, like East US or West Europe, where a provider runs a cluster of data centers.

questions.q: What does an availability zone protect against?
options: Slow internet connections on the customer's end
Expired TLS certificates
A failure in one physically separate data center within a region, while other zones keep serving traffic
A failure of an entire region at once
questions.explain: Availability zones are physically separate data centers within the same region, each with independent power and cooling, so a failure in one doesn't take down the others.

questions.q: Why does Northbridge Retail run its checkout service across two Azure regions?
options: To reduce their monthly bill
To protect against an entire region becoming unreachable, so checkout can keep running from the other region
Because it's required by every cloud provider
Because a single region can only host one application
questions.explain: Running across two region-paired locations protects against a rare but possible regional outage — the kind of failure a single region's availability zones can't protect against.

options: A pair of IP addresses assigned to one VM
Two availability zones within the same data center
Two geographically distant regions a provider recommends replicating critical data across
Two servers in the same data center
questions.explain: A region pair is two geographically distant regions designated by the provider for replicating data and services, protecting against a disaster that takes out an entire region.

questions.q: Why might a small internal tool run fine in just a single zone of a single region, while a checkout service should not?
options: Checkout services use a different cloud provider entirely
Internal tools are not allowed to use multiple zones
Downtime for a checkout service directly costs revenue, justifying the added cost and complexity of more resiliency
Single-zone deployments are always faster
questions.explain: More zones and regions add resiliency but also cost and complexity — worth it for a revenue-critical service like checkout, less necessary for a low-stakes internal tool.
